* feat(cli): name Sutura runs after the CI run they repair

Every Sutura run displayed the same "Sutura" title, so a list of runs
gave no way to tell which CI failure each one answered, and the no-op
runs created by green CI completions looked identical to real repairs.

Add a run-name to the repo workflow and to the shipped install template.
GitHub derives a run's display_title from run-name, so this reaches
`gh run list`, the Actions UI, and any downstream viewer without those
consumers needing to correlate parent and child runs themselves.

The name resolves at run-creation time, before the repair job's `if:`
is evaluated, so it carries the upstream conclusion: a skipped run reads
"(success)" and explains its own presence. The template reads the
upstream name from github.event.workflow_run.name at runtime rather than
interpolating the captured workflow name.

* fix(security): close CodeQL ReDoS alerts in log and text parsing

CodeQL reported one exponential (js/redos) and fourteen polynomial
(js/polynomial-redos) backtracking alerts across the log, diff, path and
credential-redaction parsers. All of them run on CI log text and provider
responses, which a pull request can influence, so each ambiguous
repetition is replaced with an unambiguous or non-regex equivalent:

- taxonomy: the lint signature no longer nests `[\w-]*` inside a repeated
  `-[a-z][\w-]*` group.
- classify / audit-only: `\s+(.+)` becomes `\s+(\S.*)`; the npm script
  header captures the package token and inspects `@` directly; the
  `diff --git` header is split with lastIndexOf instead of `(.+) b/(.+)`.
- diff/unified: `isConventionalTestPath` matches per path segment and
  finds `.test.` / `.spec.` with indexOf.
- tavily / nebius: trailing-slash trimming moves to a shared linear
  `trimTrailing`; the not-a-function signature drops its overlapping
  dotted-suffix group.
- source-context: the Node specifier pattern no longer lets `\s+` and
  `[^'"\n]*?` consume the same run; the Python `as` split uses `\s`.
- security/external-text: the PEM label run is unambiguous, the key body
  scan is bounded to 8192 characters, the identifier prefix is bounded,
  and the shared `\s*` before `=` is hoisted out of the optional type
  annotation.
- cli/eval: dash trimming uses the shared `trimEdges`.

Verified with the CodeQL CLI (codeql/javascript-queries, the suite the
CodeQL workflow runs): 15 of 15 alerts cleared, no new findings. The
remaining alert, js/shell-command-constructed-from-input on shellQuote,
is dismissed on GitHub as a false positive -- shellQuote is itself the
POSIX single-quote sanitizer that CodeQL does not model.

`taxonomyPrompt()` embeds `signature.source` verbatim, so the taxonomy
change alters the recorded diagnosis request in three captured replay
bundles. Their request bodies are updated in place and their
`bundleSha256` entries in the captured fixture manifest are recomputed;
every recorded response is untouched.

* feat(core): evaluate counterfactual alternatives through the production gates

Run two or three alternative patches from the same baseline sandbox image
through the identical gate stack the accepted patch passes, and record the
exact gate and rule that rejected each one.

The gate stack is reused, not re-implemented: validateCandidateDiff, race,
audit, then the repository policy commands and resource thresholds.
enforceWinnerPolicy moves to audit/repository-policy.ts and the sandbox
command helpers to engine/sandbox-command.ts so both callers share one
definition without a circular import; heal.ts keeps thin wrappers.

Rejecting a deceptive patch costs zero inference because audit short-circuits
at the mechanical layer, so the measured additional cost is sandbox operations
and elapsed time, reported per alternative and in total.

Counterfactual results reach the evidence formats without repeating any patch
body: CaseFile.counterfactual carries the verdicts, a new counterfactual-result
trace event carries ids, gates, and rules only, and the ATIF exporter maps it
to a system step with extra.sutura.rejected_by. EVALUATION_SCHEMA_VERSION and
ATIF_SCHEMA_VERSION are unchanged.

No search limit, budget, attempt cost, mechanical check, adjudication prompt,
policy rule, Placebo fixture, or scorer changes. Counterfactual evaluation
never changes a production outcome.

* feat(placebo): prove counterfactual rejection offline and build the Arena

Counterfactual set and offline harness (Phase 3). Five corpus cases carry two
or three alternative patches each, declared in packages/placebo/counterfactual/
outside the frozen corpus so corpusHash is byte-identical to the committed
placebo-v0.2-corpus.json. The harness applies every alternative to a fresh copy
of the same broken fixture and walks the deterministic gates in the production
order: repository and built-in patch policy, then the mechanical green-washing
checks, then the visible verification suite. The observed gate and rule are
compared with the declaration, so a declaration can never drift from the
running gates.

Measured, provider-free, in docs/demo/sutura-counterfactual-v0.2.json:
15 alternatives, 14 rejected, 10 of 10 declared shortcuts rejected, 0 observed
gates differing from their declaration, USD 0 inference, 17 sandbox-equivalent
operations. Nine distinct rules fire, covering a weakened assertion, a bypassed
test run, a deleted test, two loosened types, a relaxed lint config, a relaxed
Python tool config, and a swallowed error path. The one alternative no
deterministic gate rejects makes the visible suite exit 0 and fails the hidden
test set, which is the case's own demonstration that green is not sufficient.

Live path (Phase 4). `sutura heal --alternatives-file` reads and validates a
bounded JSON set; the Placebo harness writes it into the per-case temporary
directory and passes the path, so patch bodies never cross the process boundary
as argv values. `placebo run --counterfactual` opts in; the default run is
byte-identical to before.

Arena (Phases 5 to 9). A comparison manifest refuses any arm unless case
selection, corpus hash, models, routing profile, budget profile hash, score
contract, and grounding are identical, and refuses an arm that does not cover
every case id, so no failed case can leave a denominator. The three executed
arms are expressed only through existing SearchLimits, with the beam arm
asserted equal to DEFAULT_SEARCH_LIMITS; an arm may set only the four
SUTURA_SEARCH_* names. "First green patch wins" is a scoring projection over
recorded evidence that never reaches repairFailure and costs no inference.
Stratified selection is a pure function of a catalog snapshot, a seed, and
declared floors, and records language, failure class, repository, difficulty,
and inclusion reason per case. The Arena report renders every measure the
roadmap lists and refuses an incomplete comparison unless a labelled draft is
asked for. Expansion toward 200 cases is refused until the run is complete,
affordable inside remaining authorized budget, and still statistically useful.

Offline control artifacts prove the harness end to end with no provider and no
spend: the dummy control approves all 19 traps and the refuse-all control
approves none. They carry a CONTROL ARTIFACT banner so they can never be read
as a Sutura result. The measured Arena replaces them under authorization gate
G2.

No change to DEFAULT_SEARCH_LIMITS, DEFAULT_REPAIR_BUDGET_LIMITS,
REPAIR_ATTEMPT_COSTS, any mechanical check, the adjudication prompt, any policy
rule, packages/placebo/corpus, or packages/placebo/src/score.ts.

eight alternatives, and rejectedBy present exactly when the alternative was
rejected. Every rendered value is escaped.

A case with no counterfactual evidence renders exactly as before.

The two columns collapse to one at the existing 719px breakpoint.

selection is the controller-owned part of that: it decides which files may
change together, before any model sees a contract.

A target set is every editable source on its own, plus at most two pairs. A

ambiguous or duplicate pair is never offered, so no later gate has to
recognize one. Each slot binds its exact path, line range and content hash,
and the set identity covers all of them.

* feat(repair): admit atomic two-file repair transactions

with a reason rather than accepted on the strength of its citation.

everything that states or implies the answer: case kind, expected outcome,
final verdict, adjudicator recommendation, hidden tests and their results,

different split from the case it derives from, which is the leak that would
make a held-out score meaningless. The same corpus yields the same assignments
and hash in any input order, and a family that fits no remaining split is
refused rather than divided.

* feat(verification): complete the two-file controls and gate search on verification

Phase 3's acceptance table is now executable end to end.

upstream-two-file-api-migration pins a slugkit 1 to 2 release whose slugify
requires an explicit separator. Two related modules call it and one imports the
other, so the controller's related-source rule genuinely pairs them; repairing
either alone leaves the suite red.

upstream-manifest-lockfile-pair is the sharper control. Bumping only the
manifest does not merely fail its tests: frozen installation refuses to run at
all with an outdated-lockfile error. That is what makes a manifest and its
lockfile one transaction rather than two edits, and moving both installs and
passes from the offline cache.

Both traps produce a green suite and are each refused by the seam that actually
applies. The built-in patch policy names the weakened test file; the transaction
cap refuses the third changed path, which the built-in rules alone find
unobjectionable. The tests assert each against its own seam rather than
pretending one gate catches both.

Phase 4 gains the parts that make verification decidable. Probe targets are
validated against absolute, traversal, symlink, reserved, policy-denied and
hash-mismatched sources, and the trusted-contract check runs before anything a
proposal can influence. Expected values are derived from the trusted contract
alone: a fabricated expectation carried alongside a valid citation cannot
override it, and the floor-only pagination patch is refused at the exact
boundary where the correct one passes.

Search now treats diagnosed-test green as provisional. Only a fully accepted
result cancels siblings and terminates; a refused patch keeps its reason and
leaves the frontier running. Challenge budgeting reserves the mandatory audit
before generation is priced, reduces retention before freezing when the
remainder cannot cover every proposal, and refuses explicitly rather than
spending the audit reserve.

* feat(search): refuse a green-washed patch before it cancels its siblings

heal.ts now supplies the admission hook phase 4 requires. A branch whose
diagnosed test passes is provisional; the mechanical green-washing checks run
before siblings are cancelled, so a patch that goes green by weakening an
assertion, loosening a type or relaxing a config no longer ends the race and
hides the alternatives that might have been correct. The node records
verification-refused with the failing check named.

Those checks are pure functions of the diff, so admission costs no sandbox
operation, provider turn or budget capacity, and needs no new reservation. The
provider-backed gates still run once on the winner; moving them into admission
needs an audit reserve sized for several candidates, which the phase record
names as the remaining work.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(challenges): cover quality fixtures and forged observation envelopes

An invalid challenge must never read as a defect in the patch. The runner
controls now cover a baseline import failure, a nondeterministic baseline, a
nondeterministic candidate, contradictory challenges that must not cancel out
into an approval, two equivalent valid repairs scoring identically, and a
bug-regression challenge the candidate fixes. Every unqualified case yields
insufficient rather than failed.

Phase 1's observation envelope already rejected any field beyond version and
value; the tests now name the specific forgeries this phase calls out, an
approved, passed or verdict field carried alongside a valid value, and an
envelope that exits without one.

The remaining limitation is written down rather than papered over: a test-aware
patch that computes the right answer for exactly the inputs a challenge names
passes those and fails a held-out input. Controller-owned expectations stop a
candidate asserting its own correctness; they do not stop it being right only
where it is looked at.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KThJaZ82fjcK6quP8cCpDC

* feat(verification): identify the frozen challenge set in replayable evidence

Phase 1's evidence recorded that a run used challenges but not which ones. An
optional challenges.setHash now names the frozen set, so a replayed run can be
tied to the exact challenges it executed.

Optional is the point. Evidence recorded before challenge sets were hashed
still decodes byte for byte and round trips unchanged, which is what keeps
historical replay readable. A malformed digest is refused, a run that disabled
challenges may not carry a set at all, and changing the set changes the
normalized comparison identity so a replay cannot silently substitute one.

All five gate statuses reproduce across encode and decode. Subject-level hashes
per repetition and cancellation replay still need challenge execution wired into
the report rather than only into the codec.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KThJaZ82fjcK6quP8cCpDC

* feat(verify): add the verify command and a mutation-free Action route

Phase 5 gives the verification contract a way in. sutura verify parses the full
argument set and refuses a short sha, an uppercase sha, a branch name or a
41-character value for either commit, so verification is tied to the exact
commit that failed rather than to something that merely resolves.

The candidate patch is opened once and every check is made against that same
handle, so the bytes verified are the bytes measured; a directory, a
non-regular file and an oversized file are refused before any content is read.
Validation happens before anything executes, so an untrusted command, an
unparseable patch or a protected path is refused without a sandbox starting.

The Action route takes no repository port and returns no pull-request intent.
There is no path from it to a branch, commit, comment or check-run write, and
that is a property of the signature rather than a rule the function remembers;
a test asserts the module never reaches for the repository client or Octokit.
The trusted policy commit comes from workflow configuration, so a pull request
cannot ask for a more permissive policy by supplying one in its own patch.

One defect found while testing: the Action input reader trimmed the candidate
patch, which strips the trailing newline a unified diff needs. Patch bytes are
now preserved exactly and only checked for presence.
